title: Who the Denisovans were and how far they ranged
summary: Known mostly from DNA and a handful of fossils at seven locations, Denisovans may be a separate species or an archaic subspecies; their full range rests largely on DNA traces in living people.
why: Their genes live on in many modern people, yet their body and homeland are barely known.

notes.problem: Source lead gives approximately 200,000-32,000 years ago, not 50,000.

question: Who exactly were the Denisovans, what did they look like, and how far did they range?
evidence: Fossils from Denisova Cave, Xiahe (Tibet), Tam Ngu Hao (Laos), Penghu, Harbin (confirmed Denisovan 2025); some East Asian archaic fossils may or may not belong to them.
wouldSettle: More DNA- or protein-identified skeletons, especially complete skulls and finds from Southeast Asia.

theories.name: A distinct Homo species
theories.idea: Denisovans were their own species, now tied to fossils like the Harbin skull.

theories.name: Archaic subspecies of Homo sapiens
theories.idea: They were a subspecies within our own species rather than a separate species.
